dominant_strengths: Authentic editor preview with real syntax tokens demonstrates the product viscerally and reinforces credibility through code-level craft
Restrained dark palette with a single saturated blue accent gives the headline gravity and unifies CTA hierarchy
Subtle grid/dot scaffolding and keyboard shortcut chips signal a native, developer-respecting voice
dominant_weaknesses: Headline gradient blue feels generic for a category drowning in 'love your editor' tropes; copy and visual lack a distinctive hook
Three-up feature row is typographically flat and visually undifferentiated, reading as filler between hero and demo
Vertical rhythm between hero, feature row, and editor screenshot is cramped, with the demo getting cut off awkwardly at fold
fix_priorities: Sharpen positioning copy and add a distinguishing visual motif beyond gradient text to escape Linear/Cursor sameness
Give the feature trio iconography, dividers, or asymmetric layout to earn its vertical space
Rebalance hero-to-demo spacing so the editor screenshot anchors with intentional reveal rather than abrupt clipping
rationale.norman_balance: Behavioral clarity (download paths, shortcuts, real code) leads, visceral is competent-but-familiar, and reflective meaning is thin beyond 'fast Rust editor'.
rationale.intent_fit: Yes—it reads unmistakably as a modern devtools landing page for a code editor, just within a crowded stylistic convention.
